context.title: Ordaining the Priests
context.summary: A seven-day ceremony ordains Aaron and his sons with washing, clothing, anointing and sacrifices; then God commands a lamb every morning and evening and promises to dwell among Israel.
context.background: The Hebrew phrase for ordaining a priest is literally 'to fill the hand' (v. 9), perhaps referring to offerings placed in the priest's hands (v. 24).

customs.term: Blood on ear, thumb and toe
customs.note: Blood was put on the right ear, right thumb and right big toe, consecrating the priest's hearing, work and walk to God's service.
Portions were lifted and moved before the altar, presenting them to God before they were burned or given to the priests.

watchFor: The daily offering, morning and evening (vv. 38–42).
The goal: 'I will dwell among the children of Israel, and will be their God' (v. 45).

w: and you will make a sin offering
and it will be shown as holy

people.name: Aaron
people.summary: The eldest son of Amram and Jochebed, a daughter of Levi (Ex. 6:20). Some explain the name as meaning mountaineer, others mountain of strength, illuminator.

people.name: Israel
people.summary: One who follows on another’s heels; supplanter, (Gen. 25:26; 27:36; Hos. 12:2-4), the second born of the twin sons of Isaac by Rebekah. He was born probably at Lahai-roi, when his father was fifty-nine and Abraham one hundred and fifty-nine years old.

places.name: Holy Place
places.summary: One of the two portions into which the tabernacle was divided (Ex. 26:31; 37:17-25; Heb. 9:2). It was 20 cubits long and 10 in height and breadth.

places.name: Egypt
places.summary: The land of the Nile and the pyramids, the oldest kingdom of which we have any record, holds a place of great significance in Scripture.
